purpose: Phase-7C Section 4 regulatory T-cell (Treg) runtime coefficients. Estimates the SUPPRESSIVE INFLUENCE Tregs exert on the adaptive response (not full Treg biology). Recruitment / infiltration / activation / suppressive competence / suppressive persistence are separable; a recruited population may fail to infiltrate, and highly suppressive cells may persist despite declining activation. Tregs never mutate CD8/CD4 objects - they publish contribution objects. All weights + temporal constants registry-driven; prediction-only; schematic [0,1].

persistence.note: suppression persists after initiating conditions decline; gradual decay + recurrence, registry-driven.

suppression_targets.note: each target receives a SEPARATE, uniquely-identified suppressive contribution.

coefficient_policy.source: general regulatory-T-cell suppression biology applied predictively
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: suppressive competence is independent of activation (a Treg may be activated but only moderately suppressive).
coefficient_policy.limitations: No Treg count / FOXP3 / cytokine level (all NOT_REPORTED).
